title: Emperor Guangwu of Han issues the King of Na gold seal
description: The King of Na Gold Seal was issued by Emperor Guangwu of Han to an envoy from the Japanese state of Na in 57 AD. Nakoku may have been the leading state of a coalition of states in northern Kyushu in the 1st century AD. The seal provides the first historical record of a Japanese state and of diplomatic relations between China and Japan. The seal was discovered on Shikanoshima Island in Hakata Bay in 1784.

title: Taika Reforms
description:
Emperor Kotoku announces the Taika reforms, major political reforms led by Prince Naka no Ōe that centralized power under the Imperial Throne and introduced changes to the administrative system. These reforms would be implemented over the course of the coming years

It contained four main articles:

Article 1 abolishes older Japanese ranks and titles to land and people.

Article 2 creates a capital region where the government is to be based and creates outer provinces and districts to be ruled by appointed governors.

Article 3 orders a survey of land and people so that families can be assigned a parcel of land to cultivate.

Article 4 abolishes older taxes, including an unpopular labour corvee, and establishes a new system of taxation.

Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Establishment of Heijō-kyō (Nara)
description: Japan establishes its first permanent capital city at Heijō-kyō, modeled after the Tang dynasty capital of Chang'an.

title: Smallpox Epidemic of 735-737
description: A smallpox epidemic emerged in Dazaifu in Kyushu that probably origated from traders or mariners who returned from Korea. Over the next 2 years, the disease would spread all across the country and would extinguish one million lives, which was approximately a third of the Japanese population at the time. The epidemic even impacted the nobility, with the Fujiwara clan losing some of its influence at court due to the deaths of four of its leading kinsmen. It took several years for the country to recover.

title: Consecration of the Great Buddha at Tōdai-ji
description: Emperor Shōmu completes the massive bronze Great Buddha (Daibutsu) at Tōdai-ji to promote peace and ward off epidemics.

title: Saicho founds the Enryaku-ji Temple on Mount Hiei
description:
Saicho founded the Enryaku-ji temple on Mount Hiei, which overlooked the capital of Heian-kyo to the northeast. After Saicho returned from studies in China, the temple became a center for the Tendai sect of Buddhism he transmitted from China. According to Chinese geomancy, the life force of ki flowed from the northeast to the southwest; the temple therefore had a duty to purify this force from sinful pollutants through prayer and religious devotion before it progressed to the capital.

The prestige of the institution as a center of profound learning and its role in protecting the fortunes of the city from malign forces made it influential to the ruling elite; elites in the capital would often commission the temple for Buddhist court services, and sometimes the temple played on the elites' religious superstitions to maintain their interests.

title: Capital Moves to Heian-kyō (Kyoto)
description: Emperor Kanmu moves the Imperial court to Heian-kyō, marking the beginning of the classical Heian Period and a golden age of arts and literature.

title: Battle of Dan-no-ura
description: The Minamoto clan decisively defeats the Taira clan in a major naval battle, bringing an end to the Genpei War and ending imperial political dominance.

title: Establishment of the Kamakura Shogunate
description: Minamoto no Yoritomo is granted the title of Shogun, formalizing Japan's first military samurai government.

title: First Mongol Invasion (Battle of Bun'ei)
description: Kublai Khan's fleet invades Hakata Bay, but the samurai forces hold out until a severe storm forces the invaders to retreat.

title: Second Mongol Invasion (Kamikaze)
description: A massive Mongol fleet attempts a second invasion at Hakata Bay but is completely destroyed by a legendary typhoon known as the 'Kamikaze' (Divine Wind).

title: Outbreak of the Ōnin War
description: A succession dispute plunges Kyoto into brutal civil war, devastating the capital and launching the chaotic Sengoku (Warring States) period.

title: Arrival of Portuguese and Matchlock Guns
description: Portuguese traders shipwreck on Tanegashima, introducing matchlock firearms to Japan and dramatically revolutionizing Japanese warfare.

title: Battle of Okehazama
description: Oda Nobunaga executes a surprise lightning raid to defeat the vastly superior army of Imagawa Yoshimoto, establishing himself as a key unifier of Japan.

title: Honnō-ji Incident
description: Oda Nobunaga is betrayed by his general Akechi Mitsuhide and forced to commit seppuku in Honnō-ji temple, setting off Toyotomi Hideyoshi's rise.

title: Establishment of the Tokugawa Shogunate in Edo
description: Tokugawa Ieyasu is appointed Shogun and establishes the central administration at Edo Castle, initiating over 250 years of domestic peace.

title: Siege of Osaka Castle
description: The Tokugawa Shogunate destroys the Toyotomi clan at Osaka Castle, eliminating the last major military threat to its rule.

title: Shimabara Rebellion
description: An uprising of Christian peasants on the Shimabara Peninsula is crushed, leading directly to strict enforcement of national isolation (sakoku).

title: Commodore Perry's Black Ships Arrive
description: US Commodore Matthew Perry arrives in Uraga Harbor with steam-powered warships, forcing Japan to end two centuries of isolation and open its ports.

title: Meiji Restoration
description: The last Shogun, Tokugawa Yoshinobu, hands political power back to Emperor Meiji, initiating rapid modernization and westernization in Japan.

title: Promulgation of the Meiji Constitution
description: Japan adopts Asia's first modern parliamentary constitution, creating the Imperial Diet and establishing a constitutional monarchy.

title: First Sino-Japanese War
description: Conflict over dominance in Korea leads to war with Qing Dynasty China, establishing modernized Japan as a major regional power.

title: Queen Himiko Sends Envoy to Wei Dynasty China
description: Queen Himiko of Yamatai dispatches a diplomatic delegation to the Cao Wei court in China, receiving official recognition and gold seals.

title: Official Introduction of Buddhism to Japan
description: King Seong of Baekje in Korea sends a bronze statue of Buddha and sutras to Emperor Kinmei, sparking the adoption of Buddhism in Japan.

title: Battle of Shigisan (Soga-Mononobe Conflict)
description: Soga no Umako defeats Mononobe no Moriya at Mount Shigi, clearing the way for Buddhism to become central to court policy.

title: Prince Shōtoku Issues Seventeen-Article Constitution
description: Prince Shōtoku promulgates a moral and administrative code based on Confucian ethics and Buddhist principles.

title: Battle of Baekgang
description: Combined Tang Dynasty and Silla forces defeat Japanese forces attempting to restore the Korean kingdom of Baekje.

title: Jinshin War Succession Crisis
description: A bloody succession dispute erupts after Emperor Tenmu overthrows his nephew Prince Ōtomo to claim the Imperial throne.

title: Completion of the Kojiki
description: O no Yasumaro presents the Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters) to Empress Genmei, codifying Japanese myth, lineage, and history.

title: Kūkai Founds Mount Kōya Monastic Complex
description: Monk Kūkai (Kōbō-Daishi) establishes the Shingon esoteric Buddhist headquarters on Mount Kōya under imperial grant.

title: Fujiwara no Yoshifusa Becomes First Regent
description: Fujiwara no Yoshifusa becomes Sesshō (regent) for the child Emperor Seiwa, initiating centuries of Fujiwara clan dominance.

title: Murasaki Shikibu Writes The Tale of Genji
description: Noblewoman Murasaki Shikibu composes Genji Monogatari at court, widely considered the world's first novel.

title: Construction of Byōdō-in Phoenix Hall
description: Fujiwara no Yorimichi converts his villa into Byōdō-in temple, creating the iconic Phoenix Hall representing Amida's Western Pure Land.

title: Hōgen Rebellion in Kyoto
description: A civil conflict over imperial succession brings samurai clans (Taira and Minamoto) into central court politics as primary armed powerbrokers.

title: Heiji Rebellion and Taira Supremacy
description: Taira no Kiyomori defeats Minamoto no Yoshitomo in Kyoto, establishing the Taira samurai clan as the dominant ruling faction.

title: Jōkyū War Between Court and Shogunate
description: Retired Emperor Go-Toba attempts to overthrow the Kamakura Shogunate, but Hōjō regent forces crush the uprising and assert military control over Kyoto.

title: Kemmu Restoration Ends Kamakura Rule
description: Emperor Go-Daigo overthrows the Hōjō clan and Kamakura Shogunate with the help of Nitta Yoshisada and Ashikaga Takauji.

title: Ashikaga Takauji Founds Muromachi Shogunate
description: Ashikaga Takauji breaks with Emperor Go-Daigo, sets up a rival emperor in Kyoto, and establishes the Muromachi Shogunate.

title: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu Builds Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
description: Shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu constructs his Kitayama villa, later converted into the iconic Zen temple Kinkaku-ji.

title: Fourth Battle of Kawanakajima
description: Takeda Shingen and Uesugi Kenshin fight their most famous, bloodiest encounter at Kawanakajima in Shinano Province.

title: Battle of Nagashino Firearm Victory
description: Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu utilize volley-firing matchlock gunners behind wooden palisades to annihilate Takeda cavalry.

title: Toyotomi Hideyoshi Issues Great Sword Hunt
description: Hideyoshi disarms peasants to enforce rigid social class boundaries between samurai warriors and agricultural farmers.

title: Hideyoshi Launches First Invasion of Korea
description: Toyotomi Hideyoshi dispatches 160,000 samurai from Nagoya Castle in Kyushu to invade Korea in a bid to conquer Ming Dynasty China.

title: Battle of Sekigahara
description: Tokugawa Ieyasu's Eastern Army defeats Ishida Mitsunari's Western Army, securing Tokugawa's undisputed hegemony over Japan.

title: Tokugawa Shogunate Issues Sakoku Edict
description: Shogun Tokugawa Iemitsu restricts foreign trade strictly to Nagasaki and forbids Japanese citizens from traveling abroad under penalty of death.

title: Dutch Trading Post Relocated to Dejima
description: The Shogunate moves the Dutch East India Company to the artificial island of Dejima in Nagasaki Harbor, establishing Japan's primary window to European science.

title: Great Fire of Meireki in Edo
description: A catastrophic fire destroys over 60 percent of Edo and claims an estimated 100,000 lives, leading to major urban replanning.

title: The Revenge of the Forty-Seven Rōnin
description: Former retainers of Asano Naganori avenge their master by killing Kira Yoshinaka in Edo before submitting to ritual seppuku.

title: Hōei Eruption of Mount Fuji
description: Mount Fuji erupts following a megaquake, showering Edo in volcanic ash and devastating surrounding agricultural lands.

title: Tokugawa Yoshimune Begins Kyōhō Reforms
description: Eighth Shogun Tokugawa Yoshimune introduces fiscal austerity measures, land reclamation projects, and relaxes bans on Western books.

title: Great Tenmei Famine
description: Eruptions of Mount Asama paired with severe weather trigger a devastating nation-wide famine claiming hundreds of thousands of lives.

title: Matsudaira Sadanobu Enacts Kansei Reforms
description: The Shogunate clamps down on merchant luxury, cancels samurai debts, and enforces Neo-Confucian orthodoxy at official academies.

title: Hokusai Publishes Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Ukiyo-e artist Katsushika Hokusai releases his iconic woodblock print series featuring 'The Great Wave off Kanagawa'.

title: Ōshio Heihachirō Rebellion in Osaka
description: Former official Ōshio Heihachirō leads an armed riot in Osaka protesting Shogunate corruption and failure during the Tenpō famine.

title: Signing of the Convention of Kanagawa
description: Japan signs its first bilateral treaty with the United States, opening Shimoda and Hakodate ports to American ships.

title: Sakuradamon Incident Assassination
description: Anti-foreign Mito samurai assassinate Shogunate Chief Minister Ii Naosuke outside Edo Castle's Sakurada Gate.

title: Satsuma-Chōshū Secret Alliance (Satchō Dōmei)
description: Sakamoto Ryōma secret-brokered an alliance between long-time rival feudal domains Satsuma and Chōshū to overthrow the Tokugawa Shogunate.

title: Battle of Toba-Fushimi (Boshin War)
description: Pro-Imperial forces equipped with modern rifles defeat the Shogunate army south of Kyoto, initiating the year-long Boshin War.

title: Abolition of the Han System (Prefecture Creation)
description: The Meiji government abolishes traditional samurai domains (han) and replaces them with centralized government prefectures.

title: Outbreak of the Satsuma Rebellion
description: Saigō Takamori leads disgruntled former samurai in Kyushu against the modernized conscript Imperial Japanese Army.

title: Outbreak of the Russo-Japanese War
description: Japan launches a surprise attack on the Russian fleet at Port Arthur, sparking a war over Manchurian and Korean dominance.

title: Great Kantō Earthquake
description: A massive 7.9 magnitude earthquake strikes Tokyo and Yokohama, causing devastating firestorms that destroy over 100,000 lives.

title: Kaga Ikkō-ikki Revolt Takes Control of Kaga Province
description: Peasants and warrior-monks adhering to Jōdo Shinshū Buddhism overthrow Governor Togashi Masachika, establishing a self-governing 'peasants' kingdom' in Kaga Province that lasts nearly a century.

title: Battle of Kuzuryūgawa
description: Asakura Norikage leads 10,000 troops to defeat an invading force of over 30,000 Ikkō-ikki religious zealots along the Kuzuryū River, securing Echizen Province.

title: Hōjō Ujitsuna Captures Edo Castle
description: Hōjō Ujitsuna seizes Edo Castle from Uesugi Tomooki during the Battle of Takanawa, expanding the Go-Hōjō clan's grip over the Kantō region.

title: Night Battle of Kawagoe Castle
description: Hōjō Tsunashige and Hōjō Ujiyasu launch a daring night raid with 8,000 men to rout an besieging coalition force of 80,000 led by the Uesugi and Ashikaga clans.

title: Saint Francis Xavier Arrives in Kagoshima
description: Jesuit missionary Francis Xavier lands at Kagoshima, introducing Roman Catholicism and European Western learning (Nanban trade) to Japan.

title: Miyoshi Chōkei Assumes Control of Kyoto
description: Sengoku warlord Miyoshi Chōkei ousts Shogun Ashikaga Yoshiteru from Kyoto, becoming the de facto military dictator of central Japan.

title: Battle of Miyajima
description: Mōri Motonari uses stealth naval tactics on Itsukushima Island to destroy the vastly superior army of Sue Harukata, establishing Mōri supremacy in Chūgoku.

title: Siege of Inabayama Castle
description: Oda Nobunaga captures Inabayama Castle from Saito Tatsuoki, renames the stronghold Gifu Castle, and declares his campaign to unify Japan ('Tenka Fubu').

title: Battle of Anegawa
description: The combined armies of Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu defeat the allied Azai and Asakura clans in a fierce riverbank engagement in Ōmi Province.

title: Oda Nobunaga Burns Mount Hiei
description: Nobunaga destroys the ancient Enryaku-ji temple complex on Mount Hiei, slaughtering thousands of warrior monks to eliminate military-religious resistance.

title: Battle of Mikatagahara
description: Takeda Shingen inflicts a crushing tactical defeat on Tokugawa Ieyasu's forces in Tōtōmi Province, delivering Ieyasu's most famous battlefield defeat.

title: Oda Nobunaga Exiles Shogun Ashikaga Yoshiaki
description: Nobunaga expels the 15th Shogun Ashikaga Yoshiaki from Kyoto, effectively ending the 235-year-old Muromachi Shogunate.

title: Completion of Azuchi Castle
description: Oda Nobunaga completes Azuchi Castle on the shores of Lake Biwa, featuring revolutionary stone architecture, lavish interiors, and defensive gun ports.

title: Surrender of Ishiyama Hongan-ji
description: After an 11-year siege, Abbot Kennyo surrenders the fortified Ishiyama Hongan-ji cathedral fortress to Nobunaga, ending major militant Buddhist resistance.

title: Battle of Yamazaki
description: Toyotomi Hideyoshi marches his army back in record time ('Chūgoku Ōkaeshi') to defeat traitor Akechi Mitsuhide just days after the Honnō-ji Incident.

title: Tensho Embassy Departs for Europe
description: Christian Daimyo Ōmura Sumitada, Ōtomo Sōrin, and Arima Harunobu dispatch four Japanese Christian youths to Rome to meet Pope Gregory XIII.

title: Battle of Shizugatake
description: Toyotomi Hideyoshi defeats Shibata Katsuie in northern Ōmi Province, solidifying his position as sole political heir to Oda Nobunaga.

title: Battle of Komaki and Nagakute
description: Tokugawa Ieyasu fights Hideyoshi's forces to a tactical standstill in Owari Province, ultimately leading to a diplomatic truce between the two warlords.

title: Toyotomi Hideyoshi Appointed Imperial Regent (Kanpaku)
description: Unable to claim the title of Shogun due to non-Minamoto lineage, Hideyoshi is adopted by the Fujiwara family and named Kanpaku by the Imperial Court.

title: Hideyoshi's Kyūshū Campaign
description: Hideyoshi leads a massive invasion force of over 200,000 troops to subjugate the Shimazu clan in Kyūshū, forcing their submission.

title: Purveyors of Bateren Edict (Expulsion of Missionaries)
description: Hideyoshi issues an edict ordering all Christian jesuit missionaries ('Bateren') to leave Japan and placing Christian conversions under domain control.

title: Siege of Odawara Castle
description: Hideyoshi surrounds and starves out the Go-Hōjō clan at Odawara Castle, successfully unifying all of Japan under his administrative authority.

title: Execution of the 26 Martyrs of Japan
description: Hideyoshi orders the public crucifixion of 26 Franciscan and Jesuit Christians at Nishizaka Hill in Nagasaki as anti-foreign policies intensify.

title: William Adams Arrives in Japan aboard De Liefde
description: English navigator William Adams shipwrecks in Bungo Province; he later becomes a trusted Western advisor and samurai to Tokugawa Ieyasu.

title: Izumo no Okuni Performs First Kabuki Dance
description: Shrine maiden Izumo no Okuni begins performing avant-garde dance dramas on the dry riverbed of Kyoto's Kamo River, giving birth to Kabuki theater.

title: Dutch East India Company (VOC) Establishes Hirado Trading Post
description: The Tokugawa Shogunate grants an official Red Seal trade permit (Shuinjō) allowing the Dutch East India Company to open a factory in Hirado.

title: Departure of the Keichō Embassy to the Americas and Europe
description: Daimyo Date Masamune sends samurai Hasekura Tsunenaga aboard the galleon San Juan Bautista on a diplomatic mission to Mexico, Spain, and Rome.

title: Promulgation of the Buke Shohatto (Laws for the Military Houses)
description: Tokugawa Ieyasu issues codes of conduct strictly regulating feudal lords (daimyo), limiting castle construction, and requiring Shogunate approval for political marriages.

title: Deification of Ieyasu and Construction of Nikkō Tōshō-gū
description: The remains of Tokugawa Ieyasu are enshrined at Nikkō Tōshō-gū; he is deified as Tōshō Daigongen ('Great Deity of the East Shining Light').

title: Sankin-Kōtai System Made Mandatory
description: Shogun Tokugawa Iemitsu formalizes alternate attendance ('Sankin-Kōtai'), forcing daimyo to live every other year in Edo, draining their wealth and preventing revolts.

title: Expulsion of Portuguese Traders
description: Following the Shimabara Rebellion, the Shogunate expels all Portuguese merchants, ending the historic Nanban trade era.

title: Keian Incident Conspiracy Uncovered
description: A plot by masterless rōnin led by Yui Shōsetsu to overthrow the Tokugawa Shogunate is exposed, forcing reforms in how masterless samurai are treated.

title: Standardization of Kan'ei Tsūhō Copper Coinage
description: The Shogunate bans all foreign currency and standardizes Kan'ei Tsūhō coins across Japan, establishing a stable national monetary system.

title: Tokugawa Tsunayoshi Issues Compassion Laws for Living Things
description: Fifth Shogun Tokugawa Tsunayoshi ('Dog Shogun') institutes strict animal welfare decrees, carrying extreme punishments for harming stray dogs and animals.

title: Matsuo Bashō Embarks on Journey recorded in Oku no Hosomichi
description: Haiku master Matsuo Bashō departs Edo for the northern provinces, composing his masterpiece travel diary 'Oku no Hosomichi' (The Narrow Road to the Deep North).

title: Peak of Genroku Cultural Renaissance
description: Urban chōnin (merchant) culture flourishes in Kyoto, Osaka, and Edo through puppet theater (bunraku) by Chikamatsu Monzaemon and novels by Ihara Saikaku.

title: Arai Hakuseki Commences Shōtoku Governance Reforms
description: Confucian scholar Arai Hakuseki advises Shogun Ienobu, recoining currency to curb inflation and regulating foreign trade limits at Nagasaki.

title: Lifting of Ban on Non-Religious Western Books
description: Shogun Tokugawa Yoshimune permits translation and study of European scientific and technical works, fueling the rise of 'Rangaku' (Dutch Studies).

title: Official Recognition of the Dōjima Rice Exchange
description: The Shogunate officially sanctions Osaka's Dōjima Rice Exchange, creating the world's first formal futures market trading system.

title: Publication of Kaitai Shinsho (New Book of Anatomy)
description: Sugita Genpaku and Maeno Ryōtaku translate a Dutch anatomical text into Japanese, marking a watershed breakthrough for Western medicine in Japan.

title: Fall of Tanuma Okitsugu and End of Mercantilist Policies
description: Senior Councilor Tanuma Okitsugu is dismissed following financial scandals and widespread public unrest triggered by the Tenmei Famine.

title: Adam Laxman Russian Expedition Lands in Hokkaido
description: Russian officer Adam Laxman lands at Nemuro in Hokkaido to return shipwrecked Japanese castaways and request trade relations with Japan.

title: Inō Tadataka Commences National Geodetic Survey
description: Surveyor Inō Tadataka begins a 17-year journey walking across Japan to produce the nation's first geometrically accurate coastline maps.

title: HMS Phaeton Incident at Nagasaki
description: British frigate HMS Phaeton enters Nagasaki Harbor under a Dutch flag, seizing hostages and forcing coastal defense modernizations.

title: The Siebold Incident
description: German physician Philipp Franz von Siebold is expelled and arrested for treason after attempting to smuggle restricted maps of Japan out of the country.

title: Morrison Incident Shelling
description: Japanese coastal artillery fires on the unarmed US merchant ship Morrison under the Edict to Repel Foreign Vessels, sparking internal domestic debate.

title: Mizuno Tadakuni Launches Tenpō Reforms
description: The Shogunate attempts economic stabilization by enforcing moral austerity, dissolving merchant guilds, and banning expensive kabuki and entertainment.

title: Ansei Purge of Imperial Loyalists
description: Tairō Ii Naosuke arrests and executes over 100 political opponents and Sonnō Jōi ('Revere the Emperor, Expel the Barbarian') activists.

title: Namamugi Incident (Richardson Affair)
description: Satsuma samurai attack British merchant Charles Lennox Richardson for failing to yield to Regent Shimazu Hisamitsu's procession near Yokohama.

title: Anglo-Satsuma War (Bombardment of Kagoshima)
description: The British Royal Navy bombards Kagoshima in retaliation for the Namamugi Incident, leading Satsuma to seek British military hardware and alliances.

title: Townsend Harris Arrives in Japan to Negotiate Treaty.
description: Townsend Harris arrives in Shimoda in August 1856 after being appointed U.S Consul General to Japan by President Franklin Pierce. He establishes the first U.S Consulate in Japan at the Gyokusen-ji in September. He intends to negotiate a far-reaching, comprehensive trade treaty between the United States and Japan.

title: Battle of Minatogawa
description: Ashikaga Takauji defeats the imperial loyalist forces of Kusunoki Masashige at Minatogawa. Masashige's legendary defeat and final stand became an enduring symbol of ultimate samurai loyalty to the throne.

title: Establishment of the Southern Court at Yoshino
description: Emperor Go-Daigo escapes Kyoto and flees into the rugged mountains of Yoshino, establishing the Southern Court in opposition to the Northern Court backer Ashikaga Takauji in Kyoto.

title: Battle of Fujishima and Death of Nitta Yoshisada
description: Nitta Yoshisada, key general for Emperor Go-Daigo and conqueror of Kamakura, is struck down in an ambush at Fujishima in Echizen Province while attempting to support local loyalist garrisons.

title: Kannō Disturbance (Kannō no Jōran)
description: A bitter internal conflict erupts between Shogun Ashikaga Takauji and his brother Ashikaga Tadayoshi, fracturing the young Ashikaga regime and prolonging the Southern-Northern war as factions switch sides.

title: Southern Court Forces Briefly Recapture Kyoto
description: Exploiting the Kannō Disturbance, Southern Court forces under Commander Kitabatake Akinobu launch a surprise offensive that temporarily drives the Ashikaga regime out of Kyoto and captures the Northern emperors.

title: Prince Kaneyoshi Secures Kyushu for the Southern Court
description: Emperor Go-Daigo's son, Prince Kaneyoshi (Kanenaga), wins the Battle of Chikugogawa, establishing firm Southern Court authority over Kyushu at Dazaifu for nearly two decades.

title: Reunification of the Northern and Southern Courts
description: 3rd Shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu brokers a treaty with Southern Emperor Go-Kameyama at Daikaku-ji, uniting the two courts and ending 56 years of dynastic division under the agreement of alternating court lineages.

title: Establishment of the Shinsengumi at Mibu
description: The Kyoto Shoshidai officially authorizes the Shinsengumi under Kondō Isami and Hijikata Toshizō to operate out of Mibu Village as a ruthless special police unit defending shogunate interests in Kyoto.

title: Ikedaya Incident
description: The Shinsengumi launch a surprise night raid on the Ikedaya Inn in Kyoto, killing and arresting several radical Chōshū Sonnō Jōi samurai who were plotting to burn down the capital.

title: Kinmon Incident (Forbidden Gate Rebellion)
description: Outraged by the Ikedaya raid, Chōshū domain troops attack Kyoto to march on the Imperial Palace, but are defeated at the Hamaguri Gate by combined Aizu and Satsuma forces led by Saigō Takamori.

title: Bombardment of Shimonoseki
description: A multinational fleet of 17 British, French, American, and Dutch warships bombards Chōshū coastal forts along the Kanmon Straits after Chōshū forces unilaterally fired upon foreign merchant ships.

title: Teradaya Incident (Assassination Attempt on Sakamoto Ryōma)
description: Shogunate police attempt to assassinate Sakamoto Ryōma at the Teradaya Inn in Fushimi shortly after he brokers the Satchō Alliance. Ryōma escapes with severe hand wounds thanks to a warning from his future wife, Narasaki Ryō.

title: Second Chōshū Expedition (Bakuchō War)
description: The Shogunate launches a second punitive military campaign against Chōshū. Equipped with modern Western rifles imported through Thomas Glover and led by Takasugi Shinsaku, Chōshū forces handily defeat the massive Shogunate army.

title: Taisei Hōkan (Return of Sovereign Power to the Emperor)
description: The 15th and final Shogun, Tokugawa Yoshinobu, formally submits his resignation to Emperor Meiji at Nijo Castle, handing administrative authority back to the Imperial Court to avoid full-scale civil war.

title: Assassination of Sakamoto Ryōma (Ōmiya Incident)
description: Bakumatsu reformer Sakamoto Ryōma and his companion Nakaoka Shintarō are brutally assassinated by pro-shogunate Kyoto Mimawarigumi swordsmen at the Ōmiya soy sauce shop in Kyoto.

title: Battle of Aizu and Fall of Wakamatsu Castle
description: Imperial Meiji forces besiege and capture Aizu-Wakamatsu Castle during the Boshin War. The siege sees the tragic mass suicide of the Byakkotai (White Tiger Force) youth samurai squad on Mount Iimori.

title: Naval Battle of Miyako Bay
description: Former Shogunate naval commander Enomoto Takeaki leads a daring boarding attempt using ironclad strategy against the modern Meiji ironclad Kotetsu at Miyako Bay in Iwate Prefecture.

title: Battle of Hakodate & Fall of the Republic of Ezo
description: Imperial forces storm Goryōkaku star fort in Hokkaido. The death of Shinsengumi commander Hijikata Toshizō and the surrender of Enomoto Takeaki mark the final end of the Boshin War and complete unification of Japan under Emperor Meiji.

title: Ansei Great Earthquakes
description: A series of major destructive earthquakes strikes Edo and surrounding regions, killing over 7,000 people and weakening the Shogunate's financial stability and political authority during an already tense diplomatic crisis.

title: Establishment of the Nagasaki Naval Training Center
description: The Tokugawa Shogunate establishes its first modern naval academy at Nagasaki with Dutch naval officers as instructors, training key future leaders including Katsu Kaishū and Enomoto Takeaki.

title: Signing of the Harris Treaty (Ansei Treaties)
description: Tairō Ii Naosuke signs the Treaty of Amity and Commerce with US envoy Townsend Harris without imperial sanction, opening Edo, Kobe, Nagasaki, and Niigata to trade and granting extraterritoriality to foreigners.

title: Execution of Yoshida Shōin
description: Chōshū intellectual and founder of the Shōka Sonjuku academy Yoshida Shōin is executed during the Ansei Purge. His anti-shogunate and imperialist teachings inspired key revolutionaries like Takasugi Shinsaku and Itō Hirobumi.

title: Opening of the Port of Yokohama
description: Yokohama officially opens as a foreign treaty port, quickly growing from a small fishing village into Japan's primary international trade hub and foreign settlement center.

title: First Japanese Embassy to the United States Dispatched
description: The Shogunate dispatches its first official diplomatic mission aboard the USS Powhatan, accompanied by the warship Kanrin Maru captained by Katsu Kaishū with Fukuzawa Yukichi on board, to ratify the Harris Treaty in Washington D.C.

title: Tosa Kin Imperial Loyalist Party (Tosa Kin imperialist party) Established
description: Takechi Hanpeita forms the Tosa Kin'nitō in Kochi, rallying radical Sonnō Jōi samurai to push the Tosa domain toward overthrowing the foreign influence and supporting the Emperor.

title: First Tozen-ji Incident
description: Anti-foreign Mito samurai attack the temporary British Legation at Tōzen-ji temple in Edo, wounding foreign diplomats and highlighting the growing danger facing Westerners in Japan.

title: Assassination of Yoshida Tōyō
description: Tosa domain reformer Yoshida Tōyō is assassinated by Takechi Hanpeita's radical loyast faction for supporting open governance and reform over the strict Sonnō Jōi anti-foreign stance.

title: Sakamoto Ryōma Flees Tosa Domain (Datsu-han)
description: Sakamoto Ryōma illegally leaves his home domain of Tosa without permission—a crime punishable by death—to operate as an unaligned rōnin political activist across Japan.

title: Kobu Gattai Marriage of Princess Kazu to Shogun Iemochi
description: Princess Kazu (Kazunomiya), sister to Emperor Kōmei, marries Shogun Tokugawa Iemochi in Edo as part of the Kobu Gattai ('Union of Court and Shogunate') policy meant to reconcile imperial court and shogunate authority.

title: Emperor Kōmei Issues Order to Expel Barbarians
description: Emperor Kōmei issues an imperial decree setting June 25, 1863, as the deadline for the expulsion of all Western foreigners from Japan, putting the Shogunate in an impossible diplomatic position.

title: Chōshū Ships Shell Foreign Vessels at Kanmon Straits
description: Acting on Emperor Kōmei's expulsion decree, Chōshū domain coastal batteries and warships open fire on American, French, and Dutch merchant ships passing through the Kanmon Straits near Shimonoseki.

title: Coupt d'État of August 18 (Shichi-kyō Ochi)
description: Satsuma and Aizu forces collaborate to expel the radical anti-foreign Chōshū faction and seven allied court nobles (including Sanjō Sanetomi) from Kyoto, shifting court politics toward moderation.

title: Formation of Takasugi Shinsaku's Kiheitai
description: Takasugi Shinsaku forms the Kiheitai ('Irregular Militia') in Chōshū, creating a modern, western-trained military unit recruited regardless of traditional samurai social caste.

title: Mito Rebellion (Tengutō Insurrection)
description: Radical Sonnō Jōi samurai from Mito domain launch an armed uprising on Mount Tsukuba demanding the immediate expulsion of foreigners, but are eventually crushed by combined Shogunate forces.

title: First Chōshū Expedition
description: Following the Kinmon Incident, the Shogunate mobilizes a massive coalition expedition against Chōshū. Weakened by the Shimonoseki bombardment, Chōshū capitulates without major fighting and executes its radical leadership.

title: Establishment of the Kameyama Shachū (Trading Company)
description: Sakamoto Ryōma establishes Japan's first modern corporation and private navy/trading firm, the Kameyama Shachū (later Kaientai), in Nagasaki to supply modern weapons to anti-shogunate domains.

title: Ee ja nai ka Popular Uprisings
description: Mass spontaneous carnival-like street dancing and religious hysteria sweep central Japan from Kansai to Edo under the chant 'Ee ja nai ka' ('Who cares?' or 'Isn't it great?'), expressing social breakdown during the dying days of the Shogunate.

title: Sakamoto Ryōma Proposes the Eight-Point Program (Senchū Hassaku)
description: While aboard a ship near Nagasaki, Sakamoto Ryōma drafts an eight-point political outline advocating the Shogun's resignation, the creation of a bicameral national assembly, a modern army/navy, and a national constitution.

title: Bloodless Surrender of Edo Castle
description: Negotiations between Imperial general Saigō Takamori and Shogunate minister Katsu Kaishū result in the peaceful handover of Edo Castle to the Imperial Army, sparing Tokyo from catastrophic destruction.

title: Battle of Ueno (Shōgitai Revolt)
description: Imperial forces led by Ōmura Masujirō crush the Shōgitai, a elite corps of pro-shogunate loyalists making a desperate last stand at Kan'ei-ji temple in Ueno during the Boshin War.

title: Empress Suiko Accedes to the Throne
description: Empress Suiko becomes Japan's first attested female monarch, ruling alongside Prince Shōtoku to establish Buddhism and centralize government authority.

title: Establishment of the Twelve Level Cap and Rank System
description: Prince Shōtoku establishes a merit-based court court system based on Confucian principles, replacing hereditary aristocratic privilege with official rank caps.

title: Ono no Imoko Sent as Envoy to Sui Dynasty China
description: Japan dispatches Ono no Imoko to Emperor Yang of Sui China, famously bearing a letter addressed from the 'Son of Heaven in the land where the sun rises'.

title: Isshi Incident (Assassination of Soga no Iruka)
description: Prince Naka no Ōe and Fujiwara no Kamatari assassinate Soga no Iruka at a court audience for envoys from the Korean states. The next day, his father, Soga no Emishi, set fire to his residence and died in the flames. Empress Kogyoku abdicated two days after the incident on July 12, and was succeeded by Emperor Kotoku.

title: Promulgation of the Taihō Code
description: The imperial court enacts the Taihō Ritsuryō code, establishing a unified legal code and administrative bureaucracy modeled on Tang China.

title: Completion of the Nihon Shoki
description: Prince Toneri presents the Nihon Shoki (Chronicles of Japan) to Empress Genshō, completing Japan's first official classical state history.

title: Fujiwara no Hirotsugu Threatens Rebellion
description: Fujiwara no Hirotsugu threatens an armed revolt in Dazaifu in a memorial sent to the Court on September 24th. He condemns his political rivals Kibi no Makibi and the Buddhist prelate Genbo, who he believed were responsible for corruption at Court.

title: Monk Ganjin (Jianzhen) Arrives in Japan
description: After five failed sea voyages and losing his eyesight, Chinese monk Ganjin arrives in Nara to establish proper Buddhist monastic ordination rules.

title: Dokyo Incident (Yusa Hachiman Shrine Oracle)
description: Court monk Dōkyō attempts to claim the imperial throne with Empress Shōtoku's backing, but is thwarted by Wake no Kiyomaro's oracle from Usa Shrine.

title: Sakanoue no Tamuramaro Subdues the Emishi
description: Appointed Seii Taishōgun, Tamuramaro defeats Emishi chieftain Aterui in northern Honshu, securing imperial control over Mutsu Province.

title: Kusuko Incident
description: Retired Emperor Heizei attempts to move the capital back to Nara and overthrow Emperor Saga, but his military conspiracy is quickly suppressed.

title: Sugawara no Michizane Exiled to Dazaifu
description: Renowned scholar and minister Sugawara no Michizane is falsely accused of treason by Fujiwara no Tokihira and exiled to Kyushu, later becoming deified as Tenjin.

title: Taira no Masakado Rebellion in the Kanto Region
description: Warlord Taira no Masakado captures eight Kantō provinces and declares himself 'New Emperor' (Shinnō) before being slain in battle by Taira no Sadamori.

title: Fujiwara no Michinaga Reaches Peak Hegemony
description: Fujiwara no Michinaga becomes Sesshō regent, marrying three daughters to emperors and famously declaring 'this world is truly my world'.

title: Nine Years' War (Zenkunen War)
description: Minamoto no Yoriyoshi and his son Yoshiie wage a brutal campaign against the Abe clan in Mutsu Province, cementing Minamoto military power in the north.

title: Emperor Shirakawa Initiates Insei (Cloistered Rule)
description: Emperor Shirakawa abdicates the throne to govern from behind the scenes as a cloistered emperor, bypassing the administrative power of Fujiwara regents.

title: Taira no Kiyomori Appointed Daijō-daizin
description: Taira no Kiyomori becomes Grand Minister of State, marking the first time a samurai warrior attains the highest civilian administrative post in court.

title: Prince Mochihito Issues Call to Arms Against Taira
description: Prince Mochihito and Minamoto no Yorimasa issue a secret imperial order calling on Minamoto clans across Japan to rise up, sparking the Genpei War.

title: Battle of Ichi-no-Tani
description: Minamoto no Yoshitsune executes a daring cavalry descent down a steep cliff face to smash Taira fortifications near Kobe.

title: Honen Founds Jōdo-shū (Pure Land Buddhism)
description: Monk Hōnen begins teaching pure devotion to Amida Buddha through recitation of the Nembutsu, launching popular mass Buddhism in Japan.

title: Eisai Introduces Rinzai Zen and Tea Culture
description: Monk Eisai returns from Song China bringing Rinzai Zen teachings and tea seeds, laying the foundations for Zen philosophy and tea rituals.

title: Shinran Founds Jōdo Shinshū
description: Shinran completes the Kyōgyōshinshō, establishing True Pure Land Buddhism emphasizing absolute reliance on Amida's grace for lay followers.

title: Dōgen Establishes Eihei-ji Temple
description: Zen master Dōgen establishes Eihei-ji in Echizen Province as the chief monastery for Sōtō Zen meditation practice (Zazen).

title: Nichiren Proclaims Risshō Ankoku Ron
description: Monk Nichiren submits his treatise to the Kamakura Shogunate, warning that natural disasters and foreign invasion will strike unless the Lotus Sutra is embraced.

title: Genkō Incident
description: Emperor Go-Daigo's plot to overthrow the Kamakura Shogunate is betrayed, leading to a brief war at Mount Kasagi and his subsequent exile.

title: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu Restores Trade with Ming China
description: Shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu accepts official tally trade (Kango Bōeki) relations with Ming Dynasty China, being recognized as 'King of Japan'. Pictured is his Chinese counterpart, the Yongle Emperor.

title: Zeami Motokiyo Formulates Noh Theater Principles
description: Dramatist Zeami writes his classic aesthetic treatise Fūshikoden under Ashikaga patronage, elevating Noh into a refined high-art form.

title: Ashikaga Yoshimasa Constructs Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion)
description: 8th Shogun Ashikaga Yoshimasa constructs Ginkaku-ji, fostering the Higashiyama culture that gave birth to ink painting, tea ceremony, and flower arrangement.

title: Hōjō Sōun Captures Odawara Castle
description: Sengoku pioneer Hōjō Sōun seizes Odawara Castle, establishing the Go-Hōjō dynasty and pioneering the model of Sengoku warlord expansion.

title: Takeda Shingen Promulgates the Kyōshō Shinshū
description: Warlord Takeda Shingen enacts a legal house code for Kai Province, regulating military obligations, land rights, and domain taxation.

title: Eiroku Incident (Assassination of Shogun Ashikaga Yoshiteru)
description: Miyoshi Yoshitsugu and Matsunaga Hisahide storm the Kyoto residence of 13th Shogun Ashikaga Yoshiteru, forcing the 'Sword-Shogun' to commit seppuku.

title: Sen no Rikyū Refines Wabi-cha Tea Ceremony
description: Grand master Sen no Rikyū designs the rustic Taian tearoom, perfecting rustic rustic rustic Wabi-cha aesthetics under Toyotomi Hideyoshi's patronage.

title: Keichō Fushimi Earthquake
description: A catastrophic earthquake strikes Kansai, completely destroying Hideyoshi's newly constructed Fushimi Castle and killing thousands across Kyoto.

title: Yamaga Sokō Exiled for Neo-Confucian Critiques
description: Military strategist Yamaga Sokō is banished from Edo after criticizing official Neo-Confucian doctrine and formulating the Bushido warrior code.

title: Sharaku Releases Kabuki Ukiyo-e Woodblock Prints
description: Printmaker Tōshūsai Sharaku publishes over 140 dynamic actor portraits in Edo within ten months before mysteriously vanishing from public record.

title: Matsuura Seizan Writes Kasshi Yawa
description: Daimyo Matsuura Seizan begins compiling Kasshi Yawa, an invaluable 100-volume collection of Edo period political anecdotes, folklore, and samurai observations.

title: Hiroshige Releases The Fifty-Three Stations of the Tōkaidō
description: Utagawa Hiroshige publishes his celebrated woodblock print series capturing travel landscapes along the grand highway linking Edo and Kyoto.

title: Charter Oath of Five Articles Promulgated
description: Emperor Meiji issues the Charter Oath at Kyoto Imperial Palace, establishing democratic principles, modernization, and international learning for the new state.

title: Capital Formally Relocated to Tokyo
description: Emperor Meiji moves his permanent imperial residence from Kyoto to Edo Castle in Tokyo, officially making Tokyo the national capital of Japan.

title: Iwakura Mission Dispatched to the West
description: A top-level diplomatic embassy led by Iwakura Tomomi, Ōkubo Toshimichi, and Itō Hirobumi departs for the US and Europe to renegotiate treaties and study modern institutions.

title: Opening of Japan's First Railway Line (Tokyo-Yokohama)
description: Emperor Meiji officially inaugurates Japan's first steam railway line connecting Shimbashi in Tokyo to Yokohama, signaling rapid technological industrialization.

title: Conscription Law Promulgated
description: Yamagata Aritomo institutes mandatory military draft for all 20-year-old males, ending the ancient monopoly of the traditional warrior class.

title: Land Tax Reform (Chiso Kaisei)
description: The Meiji government replaces traditional crop percentage rice taxation with a fixed 3% cash land value tax, securing stable state revenues.

title: Haitōrei Edict (Banning of Swords)
description: The government forbids former samurai from wearing swords in public, stripping away the defining physical emblem of the traditional samurai class.

title: Establishment of the Imperial Diet
description: The first national elections are held and the Imperial Diet convenes its first legislative session in Tokyo under the Meiji Constitution.

title: Triple Intervention
description: Diplomatic pressure from Russia, Germany, and France forces Japan to return the Liaodong Peninsula to Qing China after the First Sino-Japanese War.

title: Sannai-Maruyama Site Settlement Flourishes
description: A large-scale long-term Jōmon settlement flourishes in modern-day Aomori Prefecture, featuring large raised-floor wooden structures, pit dwellings, and complex pottery production.

title: Introduction of Wet-Rice Cultivation to Kyushu
description: Paddy field rice farming technology spreads into northern Kyushu from mainland Asia (evidenced at Itazuke and Yoshinogari sites), initiating the agricultural transition into the Yayoi Period.

title: Construction of Daisen Kofun (Tomb of Emperor Nintoku)
description: Construction reaches its peak on the massive keyhole-shaped Daisen Kofun burial mound in Sakai, highlighting central Yamato authority and elite mortuary architecture.

title: Construction of Hōryū-ji Temple
description: Prince Shōtoku oversees the founding of Hōryū-ji in Ikaruga, which remains home to some of the world's oldest surviving wooden structures.

title: Emperor Tenmu Commissions the First State History and Imperial Lineage Record
description: Following victory in the Jinshin War, Emperor Tenmu orders prince and scholars to record the imperial genealogies and ancient myths, laying the groundwork for the Kojiki.

title: Nagaoka-kyō Capital Relocation
description: Emperor Kanmu moves the capital from Nara to Nagaoka-kyō to break free from the political dominance of powerful Nara Buddhist monasteries.

title: Compilation of the Man'yōshū Completed
description: Poet Otomo no Yakamochi compiles the final volumes of the Man'yōshū ('Collection of Ten Thousand Leaves'), Japan's oldest surviving poetry anthology.

title: Enchin Establishes Jimon Branch at Miidera Temple
description: Monk Enchin consolidates the Jimon branch of Tendai Buddhism at Onjō-ji (Miidera), sparking centuries of intense military rivalry with Mount Hiei (Enryaku-ji).

title: Jōhei-Tengyō Rebellion (Fujiwara no Sumitomo Sea Piracy)
description: In tandem with Taira no Masakado's Kanto revolt, Fujiwara no Sumitomo leads a massive pirate fleet across the Seto Inland Sea against central court garrisons.

title: Later Three Years' War (Gosannen War)
description: Minamoto no Yoshiie intervenes in a succession war within the Kiyohara clan of Tohoku, consolidating Minamoto influence and securing northern wealth.

title: Shōen Private Estate System Dominates Agriculture
description: Tax-exempt private estates (shōen) controlled by noble clans and major temples surpass state-allocated lands, dismantling classical central tax administration.

title: Battle of Kurikara
description: Minamoto no Yoshinaka drives a herd of oxen with flaming torches attached to their horns into Taira lines, crushing the main Taira army in a mountain pass.

title: Battle of Yashima
description: Minamoto no Yoshitsune launches a daring surprise rear attack on the Taira stronghold at Yashima in Shikoku, where Nasu no Yoichi famously shoots a fan target off a swaying ship.

title: Minamoto no Yoritomo Purges Yoshitsune
description: Pressured by Yoritomo, Fujiwara no Yasuhira attacks his guest Yoshitsune at Hiraizumi, forcing the tragic warrior hero to commit seppuku at the Koromogawa residence.

title: Establishment of the Gokenin Vassal System
description: The Kamakura Shogunate formalizes feudal land protection (go-on) in exchange for direct military service (hōkō) from personal military vassals (gokenin).

title: Hōjō Tokimasa Becomes First Shikken (Regent)
description: Following Minamoto no Yoritomo's death, Hōjō Tokimasa seizes real administrative control of Kamakura as regent (shikken), initiating Hōjō regency rule.

title: Assassination of Shogun Minamoto no Sanetomo
description: 3rd Shogun Minamoto no Sanetomo is assassinated on the steps of Tsurugaoka Hachimangū by his nephew Kugyō, extinguishing the main Minamoto line.

title: Promulgation of the Goseibai Shikimoku
description: Regent Hōjō Yasutoki issues a 51-article feudal legal code written in accessible Japanese, establishing land and judicial standards for the samurai class.

title: Battle of Tatarahama
description: After fleeing Kyoto, Ashikaga Takauji defeats Kikuchi Taketoshi in Kyushu, rallying western samurai clans to return and conquer central Japan.

title: Battle of Shijōnawate
description: Ashikaga commander Kō no Moronao defeats Southern Court loyalist Kusunoki Masatsura (son of Masashige), advancing onward to burn the imperial residence at Yoshino.

title: Kan'ei Famine Sweeps Countryside
description: Severe cold weather, droughts, and crop failure spark widespread starvation across agricultural domains, prompting the Shogunate to impose strict agricultural regulations.

title: Establishment of the Hanseki Hōkan (Return of Land Registers)
description: Daimyo of Satsuma, Chōshū, Tosa, and Hizen voluntarily surrender their domain land registers to Emperor Meiji, paving the way for complete centralization.

title: Saga Rebellion
description: Former Justice Minister Etō Shimpei leads disgruntled former samurai in Saga in an armed uprising against Meiji Westernization before being suppressed by government troops.

title: Taiwan Expedition of 1874
description: Saigō Tsugumichi commands a punitive expedition to southern Taiwan following the murder of shipwrecked Ryukyuan sailors, marking Imperial Japan's first overseas deployment.

title: Treaty of Ganghwa Signed with Korea
description: Following gunboat diplomacy at Ganghwa Island, Japan forces Joseon Korea to sign an unequal treaty opening three Korean ports to Japanese commerce.

title: Shinpūren Rebellion in Kumamoto
description: Traditionalist samurai armed only with swords launch a surprise night attack on the government garrison in Kumamoto to protest westernization policies.

title: Assassination of Ōkubo Toshimichi
description: Home Minister and dominant Meiji oligarch Ōkubo Toshimichi is assassinated at Kioizaka in Tokyo by samurai supporters of the fallen Saigō Takamori.

title: Annexation of the Ryukyu Kingdom (Okinawa Prefecture Formed)
description: The Meiji government formally dethrones King Shō Tai, abolishing the Ryukyu Domain and incorporating the islands into Japan as Okinawa Prefecture.

title: Political Crisis of 1881 (Okuma Shigenobu Expelled)
description: Oligarchs expel Ōkuma Shigenobu from the government after he pushes for rapid British-style parliamentary elections, leading to the promise of a constitution within ten years.

title: Chichibu Incident Insurrection
description: Impoverished silk farmers affiliated with the Freedom and People's Rights Movement launch a major armed peasant revolt in Saitama against deflationary government economic policies.

title: Sino-Japanese Convention of Tientsin (Li-Itō Pact)
description: Itō Hirobumi and Li Hongzhang agree that both Japan and Qing China will withdraw troops from Korea and give prior notification before future military deployments.

title: Normanton Incident Sparks Public Anti-Treaty Outcry
description: A British cargo ship sinks off Wakayama and the British captain saves only Western crew while letting 25 Japanese passengers drown, causing national outrage over extraterritoriality laws.

title: Promulgation of the Imperial Rescript on Education
description: Emperor Meiji issues an imperial rescript laying out national moral guidelines, emphasizing filial piety, social harmony, and absolute loyalty to the throne.

title: Otsu Incident (Assassination Attempt on Czarevich Nicholas)
description: Japanese policeman Tsuda Sanzō attacks visiting Russian Crown Prince Nicholas (later Czar Nicholas II) with a saber in Ōtsu, sparking widespread diplomatic panic in Tokyo.

title: Nōbi Earthquake Causes Widespread Destruction
description: A massive 8.0 magnitude earthquake strikes Gifu and Aichi Prefectures, killing over 7,000 people and testing modern Japanese engineered infrastructure.

title: Anglo-Japanese Treaty of Commerce and Navigation Signed
description: Foreign Minister Mutsu Munemitsu successfully negotiates the abolition of British extraterritorial rights in Japan, ending decades of unequal Western treaties.

title: Battle of the Yalu River
description: The Imperial Japanese Navy's modern ironclads defeat the Chinese Beiyang Fleet near the mouth of the Yalu River, gaining naval dominance during the First Sino-Japanese War.

title: Signing of the Treaty of Shimonoseki
description: Qing Dynasty China ceded Taiwan, the Pescadores, and Liaodong Peninsula to Japan, while recognizing total Korean independence and paying substantial war indemnities.

title: Establishment of Yawata Steel Works
description: Construction begins on state-of-the-art industrial steel manufacturing plants in northern Kyushu, utilizing war indemnity funds to drive heavy military-industrial output.

title: Boxer Rebellion Joint Expeditionary Force
description: Japan dispatches 20,000 troops as the largest component of the Eight-Nation Alliance force to lift the siege of foreign legations in Beijing.

title: Signing of the Anglo-Japanese Alliance
description: Britain and Japan form a historic military alliance in London to counter Russian expansionism in East Asia, marking Japan's entry into Great Power diplomacy.

title: Battle of Port Arthur
description: Admiral Tōgō Heihachirō launches a surprise torpedo night attack on Russian warships stationed at Port Arthur, initiating the Russo-Japanese War.

title: Battle of Mukden
description: Over 600,000 Japanese and Russian soldiers engage in one of the largest land battles in history prior to WWI, ending in a strategic victory for Field Marshal Ōyama Iwao.

title: Battle of Tsushima
description: Admiral Tōgō Heihachirō's flagship Mikasa annihilates the Russian Baltic Fleet in the Tsushima Strait, achieving a decisive naval war victory.

title: Signing of the Treaty of Portsmouth
description: Brokered by US President Theodore Roosevelt in New Hampshire, the treaty ends the Russo-Japanese War and recognizes Japan's paramount interests in Korea and southern Sakhalin.

title: Hibiya Riots in Tokyo
description: Outraged by the lack of financial war indemnities in the Treaty of Portsmouth, angry crowds riot in Hibiya Park, declaring martial law across Tokyo.

title: Establishment of the South Manchuria Railway Company (Mantetsu)
description: Japan establishes Mantetsu to operate economic development, coal mines, and transport infrastructure along its strategic Manchurian railway corridor.

title: High Treason Incident (Kōtoku Shūsui Plot)
description: Anarcho-socialist thinker Kōtoku Shūsui and eleven accomplices are arrested and executed for allegedly conspiring to assassinate Emperor Meiji.

title: Japan-Korea Annexation Treaty Signed
description: Resident-General Terauchi Masatake oversees the formal annexation of Korea, making it a Japanese territory under the Government-General of Korea.

title: Passing of Emperor Meiji and End of the Meiji Era
description: Emperor Meiji passes away after a 44-year reign that transformed feudal Japan into an industrial world power, ushering in the Taishō era.

title: Emperor Go-Daigo is exiled to the Oki Islands
description: After his plot against the Kamakura shogunate was revealed, Go-Daigo was captured and exiled the Oki Islands off the Japan Sea coast near Izumo province.

title: Departure of the First Japanese Embassy to Tang China
description: Inugami no Mitasuki and Yakushi no Enihi depart Japan on a tributary mission to the Tang Chinese court. They arrived the next year and had an audience with Emperor Taizong, who relaxed the frequency of tribute missions after learning of the embassy's long journey.

title: Emperor Jomei Moves to New Palace at Okamoto
description: Emperor Jomei moves into Okamoto Palace in the vicinity of Asuka. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: The Japanese Embassy under Mitasuki returns to Japan
description: Mitasuki's Embassy to the Tang Court returns to Japan escorted by Tang envoy Ko Hyojin. They landed on the island of Tsushima in the 8th month of the lunar calendar. They were received at the harbour at Naniwa in the 10th month with ceremony and returned to China in the new year, being escorted as far as Tsushima. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Solar Eclipse Occurs on Lunar New Year
description: The Nihon Shoki records a solar eclipse occuring on the 1st day of the 1st month. However, no such eclipse occured in 636 that was visible in Japan.

title: Emperor Jomei moves to Tanaka Palace
description: Emperor Jomei moves to the Tanaka Palace in Kashihara after the Okamoto Palace is destroyed by fire. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Solar Eclipse Occurs
description: A solar eclipse occurs on the 2nd day of the 3rd month of the lunar calendar. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki

title: Expedition Launched Against Emishi People in the North
description: The first recorded military expedition by the Yamato court occurs in 637 A.D. after the Emishi are described as being remiss at court. Kamitsukeno no Katana is sent to command a punitive expedition against the Emishi in the north. He reportedly faced major setbacks and was held up at a fortress in an unknown location in the northern frontier region. His forces eventually triumphed. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Emperor Jomei moves to Umayasaka Palace
description: Emperor Jomei moves into the Umayasaka Palace in Koryo. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Emperor Jomei moves to the Kudara Palace
description: Emperor Jomei again moves his residence to Kudara Palace after only a few months, and stays here until his death the following year. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki

title: Death of Emperor Jomei
description: Emperor Jomei dies at Kudara Palace in Koryo. He is succeeded by Empress Kogyoku.

title: Empress Kogyoku moves to Oharida Palace in Asuka
description: Empress Kogyoku moves from Koryo to Oharida Palace in Asuka. Oharida Palace is described as the "temporary" palace. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Empress Kogyoku moves to the Palace of Itabuki in Asuka
description: Empress Kogyoku moves to the new Itabuki Palace in Asuka after a brief residency at Oharida Palace. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Soga no Iruka orders assault on Prince Yamashiro
description: Soga no Iruka orders an assault against Prince Yamashiro at Ikaruga. The Prince reportedly left the bones of a horse in his sleeping chamber before fleeing to Mount Ikoma to the north. When Iruka's forces burnt down the Palace at Ikaruga, they found the bones among the ashes and believed them to be those of the Prince. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Death of Prince Yamashiro
description: Prince Yamashiro had fled to Mount Ikoma after the attack on his palace. He spent "four or five days" in the mountains without food or water. Not wanting to "impose a burden on the people", and not wanting it "to be said by after generations that for my sake anyone has mourned the loss of a father or mother", Prince Yamashiro decided to go to the Horyu-ji temple in Ikaruga. There, they took their own lives to avoid capture and conflict. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Capital is moved to Naniwa
description: The Capital is moved to Naniwa  in on the 9th day of the 12th month of the lunar calendar (which corresponds to January 1, 646). Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: New Cap and Rank System is Instituted
description: A new cap and rank system was introduced which superseded the system introduced in 603. This new system consisted of 7 cap-ranks with 13 grades. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: New Cap and Rank System is Revised
description: The old cap and rank system was discontinued in the summer of 648, and the new system was the subject of a revision in the 2nd month of the lunar year. This new system consisted of 19 grades. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Registers of Population and Land Organisation System Announced
description:
According to the Nihon Shoki, In the 4th lunar month of 652, registers of population were prepared and a system of land organisation was implemented.

"In this month the registers of population were prepared. Fifty houses were made a township, and for each township there was appointed an elder. The senior member of the family was always made the head of the household. The houses were all associated in groups of five for mutual protection, with one elder to supervise them one with another".

title: Death of Soga no Kurayamada no Ishikawa no Maro
description: After being accused of treason, Soga no Kurayamada no Ishikawa no Maro fled to the Yamada-dera temple. There, he and his family committed suicide. After his death, the allegations of treason were proven to be false, and he was posthumously pardoned. His death marked the end of the Soga clan's political relevancy.

title: Prince Naka no Oe returns to Asuka
description: Prince Naka no Oe petitioned the Emperor to move the capital back to Asuka, but the Emperor refused. A rift seemed to open between the Emperor and the Prince, and it followed that the Prince ignored the Emperor's refusal and returned to Asuka on his accord, an act the Emperor resented. Many other court nobles followed the Prince back to Asuka. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Death of Emperor Kotoku
description: Emperor Kotoku dies on the 10th day of the 10th lunar month of 654. He is succeeded by the former Empress Kogyoku, who reigns now as Empress Saimei. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Empress Saimei is Enthroned at Itabuki Palace
description: The former Empress Kogyoku takes the throne as Empress Saimei. The Empress' reign marks the return of the capital to Asuka. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Empress Saimei moves to the Kawahara Palace.
description: After a fire burns the Itabuki Palace, Empress Saimei is moved to the Kawahara Palace, also in Asuka. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Abe no Hirafu begins Expedition against the Emishi in the North
description: Abe no Hirafu is commissioned to lead a military expedition in the north to subjugate the Emishi. He reportedly led a fleet of 180 ships and drew them up in order of battle at Akita Bay. The Nihon Shoki states that the Emishi of Akita and Nushiro directly to the north "were struck with fear, and tendered their submission." He was successful in subduing the Emishi forces in these areas.

title: Emishi Peoples Travel to the Asuka Court to Pay Tribute
description: The Nihon Shoki records that "more than two hundred Yemishi came to Court with presents for the Empress". The Emishi visitors were granted various gifts in return, including ranks, titles, and luxury goods.

title: Abe no Hirafu campaigns against Mishihase in Hokkaido
description: Abe no Hirafu campaigns against the Michihase people at a location named Watarishima, which is described as being close to a great river. It is suggested that this battle occurred on the northern island of Hokkaido, probably somewhere near the mouth of the Ishikari river. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Baekje is subjugated by Tang Dynasty and Silla Forces
description: The Korean Kingdom of Baekje is defeated and subjugated by the Korean Kingdom of Silla, who were assisted by Tang China. Many Baekje nobles fled to Japan after the defeat.

title: Empress Saimei moves to Asakura Palace
description: Empress Saimei moves to Asakura Palace in Chikuzen Province, which is on the island of Kyushu. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Death of Empress Saimei
description: Empress Saimei dies at Asakura Palace on the 24th day of the 7th lunar month. She is succeeded by Prince Naka no Oe, but he is not enthroned as Emperor Tenji until 668. He rules instead as a regent until that year.

title: Defensive Fortifications Prepared in Western Japan in Anticipation of Retaliation
description: According to the Nihon Shoki, "In this year guards and beacon-fires were placed in the islands of Tsushima and Iki and in the Land of Tsukushi". These were probably measures taken in anticipation of a possible assault against Japan after the Battle of Baekgang the previous year.

title: Emperor Tenji Assumes the Throne
description: Emperor Tenji assumes the Throne, after a 6 year regency. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: National Census Compiled
description: A national census was compiled from registers of population in the country. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Emperor Tenmu is enthroned in Asuka.
description: Emperor Tenmu is enthroned at Asuka on the 27th day of the second lunar month. Recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Silla Defeats Gogoryeo and Establishes a Unified Korea
description: Silla defeats the Korean Kingdom of Gogoryeo and establishes a unified Korean state, marking the end of the Korean Three Kingdoms period.

title: Death of Emperor Tenmu
description: Emperor Tenmu dies on the 9th day of the 9th lunar month. He is succeeded by Empress Jito. She would reign so as to ensure that her son Prince Kusakabe would succeed to the throne. However, he died young and the boy who would become Emperor Monmu was named as the successor.

title: Asuka Kiyomihara Codes Are Promulgated
description: The Asuka Kiyomihara Codes are promulgated throughout 689. They are said to be a refinement of an earlier legal code from Tenji's reign known as the Omi-ryo, a collection of 22 volumes detailing various laws. These law codes were a precursor to the later Taiho codes and form an important basis for the Japanese legal Ritsuryo system.

title: Empress Jito is formally Enthroned
description: Empress Jito is formally enthroned on the first day of the lunar new year of 690. This three-year delay may be due to Chinese ideas about periods of mourning, during which time important state events such as enthronements of new sovereigns may be tainted by the pollution of death.

title: Capital is Moved to Fujiwara-kyo
description: Empress Jito moves to Fujiwara-kyo on the 6th day of the 12th month, and thus it becomes the new capital.

title: Empress Jito Abdicates
description: Empress Jito formally abdicates the throne. She is succeeded by Emperor Monmu. This event is the last event recorded in the Nihon Shoki.

title: Japanese Embassy Travels to Tang China
description: A Japanese Diplomatic Embassy headed by Awata no Mahito departed Japan for Tang China in 702. It arrived in the Tang capital of Chang'an in 703. This embassy was important was it was the first major diplomatic mission to China since the two countries fought each other at Baekgang in 663. The embassy brought with them a copy of the newly promulgated Taiho codes, inspired by the Tang legal codes. The envoys also requested during this embassy that their nation be referred to as "Nihon" instead of Yamato. The embassy had an audience with Empress Wu Zetian, the only female Chinese empress regnant throughout Chinese history. The embassy was well received in China, and returned the next year in 704.

title: First Wadokaichin Coinage Produced in Japan
description: Wadokaichin coins are minted in Japan during this time, and are mentioned in an order by Empress Genmei on this date. They were long believed to be the first official coinage in Japan until recently, when coins predating the Wadokaichin by 20 years, known as Fuhon-sen were discovered in Asuka.

title: Empress Genmei Issues Edict Announcing The Move of the Capital to Heijo-kyo
description: An edict is issued by Empress Genmei announcing plans to move the capital from Fujiwara-kyo to Heijo-kyo. This move would be completed two years later in 710. Recorded in the Shoku Nihongi.

title: Fort Ideha Is Established In Northen Japan near Akita
description: The Ideha fort is established on the northern frontier region somewhere near the modern city of Akita. It is from this time that the central government begins the subjugation of the Emishi people in the northern reaches of Japan.

title: Empress Genmei Orders The Compilation of Fudoki
description: Empress Genmei ordered the compilation of fudoki in each of the provinces. Fudoki are some of the oldest records available from Japan, and they contain such information as the names of places and their etymology; land quality; the names of various towns and districts in the provinces; as well as natural resources found in provinces.

title: Yoro Codes Are Compiled by Fujiwara no Fuhito
description: The Yoro Codes are drafted up by Fujiwara no Fuhito, and are an extension and revision of the earlier Taiho codes. They are not promulgated until almost 40 years later in 757.

title: Hayato Rebellion
description: The Hayato people, who inhabited southern Kyushu on the periphery of the Yamato state, launched a rebellion after the state attempted to enforce the Ritsuryo legal system in Hayato provinces. The rebellion lasted into 721, when the Hayato were defeated by the Yamato forces. Thereafter, the Yamato population in Kyushu increased while the Hayato gradually assimilated into Yamato society.

title: Emperor Shomu is Enthroned
description: Emperor Shomu is enthroned as Emperor in Nara.

title: Taga Castle Is Constructed
description: Taga Castle is constructed near modern-day Sendai and serves as an important base for Japanese northern frontier forces in the campaigns against the Emishi and expansion into northern Honshu.

title: Yamato Court Gains Complete Control Over Kyushu
description: After the defeat of the Hayato, Kyushu is controlled and administered entirely by the Nara court.

title: Japanese Naval Force Defeated Off Coast of Silla
description: Korean records that in 731 (30th year of King Seongdeok), "300 Japanese military ships crossed the sea and raided our eastern border, but the king ordered a longevity to send an army and greatly disrupted it."

title: Kaifuso Poetry Anthology Completed
description: The Kaifuso poetic anthology is completed, one of the oldest Japanese anthologies of poetry. It contains poems written by Japanese poets in Chinese script, which was used to represent the Japanese syllabary.

title: Fujiwara no Nakamaro Quells Opposition
description: Fujiwara no Nakamaro repulses an attempt by Tachibana no Naramaro to shift power away from Nakamaro.

title: Yoro Codes Are Implemented
description: The Yoro codes created in 718 by Fujiwara no Fuhito are finally promulgated and completes the implementation of Ritsuryo law.

title: Rebellion of Fujiwara no Nakamaro
description: Fujiwara no Nakamaro, in league with Emperor Junnin, leads a rebellion against the former Empress Koken. He was killed in battle at Miozaki near Lake Biwa.

title: Thirty-Eight Years War Begins
description: The Thirty-Eight Years War against the Emishi peoples in the north of Honshu begins. The following decades would see fighting and various campaigns between the Imperial Court and the Emishi forces.

title: Otomo no Otomaro Is Given The Appointment Of Sei-i Taishogun by Emperor Kanmu
description: Otomo no Otomaro is appointed as sei-i taishogun by Emperor Kanmu. This title translates to "Commander of the Expeditionary Force against the Barbarians", and was a commission to lead the forces of the court against the Emishi. This is the first instance of the title of shogun, which would be used in later centuries as a title that signified the military de facto leader of Japan.

title: Development of Kana Syllabary
description: The Kana syllabary system, which Japanese today is written in, is developed around this time. It is traditionally attributed to the monk Kukai.

title: Shoku Nihongi Completed
description: The Shoku Nihongi, the next national history of Japan written after the Nihon Shoki, is completed.

title: Last Japanese Embassy Sent to Tang China
description: The Last Japanese Embassy to the Tang Dynasty was headed by Fujiwara no Tsunetsugu in 839. Later missions planned for the latter half of the 9th century were cancelled and never took place.

title: Nihon Koki Completed
description: The Nihon Koki, the third national history, is completed.

title: Jowa Incident
description: The Fujiwara clan strengthen their grip on the Imperial Court when the nephew of Fujiwara no Yoshifusa, who would become the Emperor Montoku, was named Crown Prince and rivals of Yoshifusa were removed from positions of power.

title: Fujiwara no Hirotsugu Begins Rebellion
description: Fujiwara no Hirotsugu officially declares himself in revolt four days after his memorial was received by the Court. Impoverished conditions on Kyushu at the time, harsh corvee duties, and general discontent among the peasants meant that Hirotsugu was able to acquire substantial support, including from the recently defeated Hayato, and raise an appoximately 10,000 strong force.

title: Yamato Court Deploys Hayato Reconnaissance Mission
description: The Yamato Court sends a reconnaissance force composed of 24 Hayato native to Kyushu ahead of their main force, which comprised 17,000 men from eastern and western Honshu. This force was the largest military force mustered by the central government in the 8th century.

title: Hirotsugu's Force Stops at Oka Headquarters
description: Fujiwara no Hirotsugu makes a stop at Oka District Headquarters in order to strengthen his forces, set up camp, and recruit more men from the province of Chikuzen.

title: Government Forces Capture Three Rebel Camps
description: Arriving at Miyako, Hirotsugu found that one of three forces he had split did not arrive, while the other was late to appear. The forces of the central government landed on Kyushu in Buzen province and capturedt the three rebel camps at Miyako, Tomi, and Itabitsu.

title: Central Government Reinforcements Arrive in Nagato Province
description: Government reinforcement troops arrive in Nagato near the town of Shimonoseki, building up the strength of the Imperial forces.

title: Allies of Hirotsugu Defect to Imperial Forces
description: Some of Hirotsugu's supporters, including four district officials, defect to the Imperial side along with some 500 mounted men.

title: Emperor Shomu Issues Imperial Decree Denouncing Hirotsugu
description: Emperor Shomu issues a decree denouncing Hirotsugu that is distributed across Kyushu. He offers rewards for the killing of Hirotsugu.

title: Battle of Itabitsu River
description: The Imperial forces met the rebel forces under Hirotsugu at the Battle of the Itabitsu River. Hirotsugu's men were unable to cross the river, and were thus defeated and fled.

title: Hirotsugu Captured
description: After his defeat, Hirotsugu attempts to flee to the Kingdom of Silla in Korea. However, his ship was pushed back by unfavourable winds and he was captured by Imperial forces on the Goto Islands near Nagasaki.

title: Emperor Shomu Leaves Nara
description: Emperor Shomu leaves Nara and travels eastwards, presumably to avoid any potential uprising that could possibly be instigated in Nara. He arrives at the village of Tsuge on November 22nd.

title: Emperor Shomu Arrives at Nabari
description: Shomu continues eastward and arrives at Nabari on November 23rd.

title: Emperor Shomu Arrives at Ao
description: Shomu travels to Ao on November 24th.

title: Emperor Shomu Arrives at Kawaguchi
description: Emperor Shomu arrives in Kawaguchi in Ise Province, where he and other nobles stay at a temporary palace, where they would stay until December 4th. It was here that he heard of Hirotsugu's death.

title: Emperor Shomu Arrives at Akasaka
description: Emperor Shomu travels to Akasaka on December 7th.

title: Emperor Shomu Arrives at Asake District
description: Emperor Shomu travels to Asake district on December 13th.

title: Emperor Shomu Arrives at Ishiura
description: Emperor Shomu travels to Ishiura on December 18th.

title: Emperor Shomu Arrives at Tagi District
description: Emperor Shomu travels to Tagi district on December 19th.

title: Emperor Shomu Arrives at Fuwa
description: Emperor Shomu travels to Fuwa on December 23rd.

title: Emperor Shomu Arrives at Yokokawa
description: Emperor Shomu travels to Yokokawa on December 28th.

title: Emperor Shomu Arrives at Inukami
description: Emperor Shomu travels to Inukami on December 29th.

title: Emperor Shomu Arrives at Gamo District
description: Emperor Shomu travels to Gamo district on December 31st.

title: Emperor Shomu Arrives at Yasu
description: Emperor Shomu travels to Yasu on January 1st of 741.

title: Emperor Shomu Arrives at Awazu
description: Emperor Shomu travels to Awazu on January 2nd.

title: Emperor Shomu Arrives at Tamanoi
description: Emperor Shomu travels to Tamanoi on Janaury 5th.

title: Emperor Shomu Moves Capital to Kuni-kyo
description: Emperor Shomu moves the capital from Nara to Kuni-kyo. This was probably to weaken the influence of the Fujiwara, who were extremely powerful in Nara, while the area around Kuni-kyo was associated with Tachibana no Moroe, the Minister of the Right.
